subject: English
passage: At three months old, when their core academic skills begin developing, homeschooled students typically receive one-on-one instruction but have limited interaction with peers their own age. Traditional classroom students, ______ learn alongside twenty to thirty classmates daily. This difference in social exposure may help explain why homeschooled and traditionally schooled children often develop distinct communication styles: from an early age, homeschooled students tend to be more comfortable with adults but less confident in peer groups.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation:
Choice C is the best answer. "By contrast" logically signals that the information in this sentence—that traditional students learn alongside twenty to thirty classmates daily—contrasts with the preceding information (that homeschooled students have limited interaction with peers their own age).

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect because "accordingly" illogically signals that the information about traditional classroom students in this sentence is in accordance with, or results from, the information about homeschooled students in the previous sentence. Instead, the information about traditional students contrasts with what came before.
